overview: This record begins in 1920 with the French-administered eastern part of former German Togoland, rather than the full earlier German colony. The French mandate was formalized in 1922, followed by UN trusteeship. Independent Togo dates from 27 April 1960.

periods.title: French administration and trusteeship
periods.summary: The map opens before the 1922 mandate; UN trusteeship later replaced that framework.

periods.title: Republic and concentrated power
periods.summary: Independence was followed by decades of rule dominated by Gnassingbé Eyadema.

periods.title: Succession and institutional change
periods.summary: The contested 2005 succession and the 2024 to 2025 constitutional changes reshaped political offices.

items.text: Togo became independent on 27 April 1960, after a period as a UN Trust Territory under French administration. Sylvanus Olympio was prime minister at independence. The colonial division is important: today’s country did not simply inherit the whole territory once labelled German Togoland.

Gnassingbé Eyadema governed for 38 years before his death in 2005. His son Faure was first installed by the military, stepped down under pressure, and then won an election marred by severe irregularities and violence. This succession changed the president without ending the ruling family’s political influence.

The 2024 constitution supplies a short French writing sample in Article 2: “Travail - Liberté - Patrie”, meaning “Work, Liberty, Homeland”. These are the words of the national motto, reproduced in a dated legal text. Togo’s many spoken languages and cultural traditions extend well beyond this official French formula.

Koutammakou stretches across northeastern Togo and northwestern Benin. Batammariba builders make earthen tower-houses known as sikien, with takienta as the singular. The buildings belong to a living cultural landscape of farming, family relationships and ritual places, not merely to an abandoned archaeological site.

The houses organize practical work vertically: animals have space on the ground floor, while granaries stand on the terrace. UNESCO describes households maintaining traditional buildings alongside newer rectangular homes. A family can adapt its housing while preserving architectural knowledge and places used in religious life.

Togolese businesswomen known as Nana Benz helped connect local cloth buyers with European manufacturers. Their influence reached beyond selling finished fabric: exclusive patterns and commercial relationships gave particular traders considerable authority. Clothing therefore tells a story about women’s enterprise as well as the people wearing it.

One print was named Santana after the influential trader Madame Santa Anna Nelly, who held exclusive rights to it. Another bird design was called Air Afrique in Togo and had different names elsewhere. The same patterned fabric could carry several stories as it moved between markets and communities.

In 2022, WHO validated Togo’s elimination of trachoma as a public-health problem. Earlier milestones covered Guinea worm, lymphatic filariasis and sleeping sickness. These were major achievements by health workers and communities; they did not mean that every infection everywhere had vanished or that surveillance could stop.

The trachoma programme linked medical work with facial cleanliness, safe water and better sanitation. The disease can damage eyes after repeated infections, so prevention reaches into everyday washing and household routines. Health progress here involved ordinary water and hygiene services as well as specialized treatment.

A WHO and UNICEF report found that the share of Togo’s schools with basic sanitation rose from 44 percent in 2016 to 65 percent in 2019. School-led hygiene work and construction programmes contributed. Even after that improvement, many classrooms still lacked the supporting facilities children needed.

The same report describes separate toilets for girls and boys, including facilities that help adolescent girls manage menstruation. Privacy and working wash facilities can determine whether a pupil can comfortably stay at school. A toilet door that closes properly deserves more credit than it usually gets.

UNICEF’s 2021 report recorded 14 family and five school latrines using biogas technology. Biodigesters could turn waste into cooking fuel, with treated residues used as fertilizer. This small programme linked sanitation with less firewood use: the toilet was being asked to do a second job.

ending.text: Togo continues as a state. International IDEA records Faure Gnassingbé moving into the powerful new office of President of the Council of Ministers in May 2025 under a changed constitutional system. Changes of office should not be confused with the disappearance of the country or its communities.
